scoring.rule: exact string match after normalizing: lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation that is not part of a number, and strip a trailing period. Nothing fuzzy, nothing graded by a model, so two people running this get the same number.
scoring.per_item: 1 if the normalized answer equals the normalized expected string, else 0

prompt: Read the text in this image. Reply with only the text, nothing else. If there is no text, reply exactly: NO TEXT
notes: Items are sourced by URL so nobody has to ship copyrighted pictures in a git repo. The downloader records the sha256 of every file it fetches, and refuses to score a run where a file's hash changed, because a moved URL would silently change the test.
Expected strings are the text a person reads off the picture, in reading order, not a caption.
A model that adds commentary around the right text scores zero on purpose. For a camera that has to speak an answer out loud, extra words are the failure.

items.license: public domain (US federal sign design), Wikimedia Commons

items.status: draft, needs the crop step written

_status: The runner and scorer work. The item set is deliberately tiny and marked as such: three items is a smoke test, not a benchmark. Adding items is the most useful contribution this suite can get, and the rule is one line of JSON per item with a stable public URL, the exact text, and the license.
